Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2a) demonstrates asymmetry in pulmonary vascularity with a smaller, oligemic right lung and prominent left hilum, which are classic radiographic signs of chronic right pulmonary artery obstruction or stenosis associated with Takayasu arteritis. This finding is consistent with the vascular involvement typical of the disease rather than an acute embolic event or bilateral edema.
